newsitem.title: USA: Republic to buy Wallace Auto for $55 million.
newsitem.headline: Republic to buy Wallace Auto for $55 million.

text.p: Republic Industries, Inc., led by Florida billionaire Wayne Huizenga, said Monday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Wallace Automotive Group in a stock deal worth about $55 million.
Wallace owns and operates Ford, Nissan, Dodge, Mitsubishi and two Lincoln-Mercury dealerships in Southeast Florida.
The deal includes all related real estate. It will be accounted for as a pooling of interests.

"The acquisition enhances our growing automotive retailing presence in Florida and represents another step in our strategy of owning dealerships in markets where we are developing AutoNation USA megastores," said Huizenga, chairman and co-chief executive of Republic.
Republic, based in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., acquired AutoNation, a used car dealership, in January.
In connection with the merger, Bill Wallace will enter into a long-term employment agreement and remain president of Wallace.
Republic also operates in the automotive, solid waste, electronic security and media industries.
Republic's stock fell 37.5 cents to $41.50 early on Nasdaq.
